newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end higher across the board.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end higher across the board.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed higher across the board on Friday, with the distant months showing particular strength, due to bullish market sentiment, local traders said.

Prices were 10 to 240 yen higher, with the benchmark May 1998 contract closing 240 yen up at 14,570 yen per tonne. The day's estimated trading volume was 33,208 lots. The spot July contract expired at 14,970 yen, down 660 yen from the previous close, with 110 lots of deliveries.
"Local investors continued to buy today," a brokerage house trader said. But the spot July contract's weaker expiry price pressured nearby months in the afternoon, traders said.
The spot July corn contract on the CBOT Project A overnight trading system stood at $2.72-3/4 per bushel at 0835 GMT, against $2.71-1/4 at Thursday's close.
Spot July CBOT soybean futures were trading at $8.50-1/4 a bushel at 0835 GMT, up from $8.41-1/2 at Thursday's close.
